note: the canonical operation registry (the four-surface parity law): emitted from internal/ops (the source) — never hand-edited; the sync test pins it

operations.summary: Validate the example configs (the CLI verb: the config schema and the examples' conformance)
The CleanerGate admission: the policy (the verified snapshot) -> the quota (this generation's window) -> the metered usage (cleaner.executions)
operations.consequence: admits or refuses the batch; the usage meters
operations.auth_requirement: the verified policy snapshot (the entitlegate's generation binding)
operations.tenant_environment_scope: the tenant bound in the verified snapshot
operations.idempotency: the check is pure; the metered usage counts once per admission
operations.occ: the snapshot's generation binding (a stale snapshot refuses)

surface_bindings.cli: -entitlement-status -entitlement-snapshot <file> (the fail-closed snapshot verification + the identity render; verified live s105/s121)
surface_bindings.k8s: in-process (the reconciler's ExecuteWithReceipt calls Admit before the delete path)
surface_bindings.mcp: the entitlement_status tool (the read-only family; the stdio posture answers the empty body when no provider is wired)

operations.summary: Execute one entitlement-gated deletion batch (policy -> quota -> metered usage -> the rate-limited delete path)
operations.consequence: deletes the matched resources; every deletion lands in the receipt
operations.auth_requirement: the service account (the controller's own identity) + the CleanerGate's verified policy snapshot
operations.tenant_environment_scope: the CRD's namespace scope (the controller's watched cluster)
operations.idempotency: the reconciler's idempotent loop (the batch re-runs converge; the entitlegate counts one execution per admission)
operations.occ: resourceVersion-guarded status writes; the idempotent reconcile loop converges re-runs
operations.destructive_ceremony: the entitlement-gated admission (policy -> quota -> metered usage) precedes every delete path; DryRun plans first

surface_bindings.k8s: the Cleanup CRD reconciliation (pkg/controller: the PolicyReconciler.ExecuteWithReceipt through the entitlegate's CleanerGate)

absent_surfaces.api: no REST deletion route BY DESIGN (a REST deletion API would be a new operation requiring its own §17 admission — never a shortcut)
absent_surfaces.cli: no operator verb exists (the controller runs headless)
absent_surfaces.mcp: no MCP tool (the task_start family is maestro's; a cleaner tool would be the new typed operation)

operations.summary: Plan one deletion batch WITHOUT effects (the DryRun behavior: the plan contract, the batch test pins delete-must-not-delete)
operations.consequence: none (the plan only — the contract test pins delete-must-not-delete under DryRun)
operations.idempotency: pure (the same input -> the same plan)
operations.occ: n/a (the same input plans the same batch)
operations.destructive_ceremony: none (the contract test pins delete-must-not-delete under DryRun)

surface_bindings.k8s: the Cleanup CRD's DryRun behavior (pkg/controller: the batch contract)

operations.summary: The liveness/readiness surface (the controller's own health)
operations.auth_requirement: the cluster-internal (the health endpoints are not auth-gated by design; the cluster boundary is the gate)

surface_bindings.cli: -health-summary (the process-local posture: version/commit/uptime; verified live s105/s121)

absent_surfaces.api: the health endpoints ARE the HTTP surface (the only one, by design)
